summary: Earth System Trend Detective is a Python application that helps users investigate what is changing in the environment, where it is changing, and how certain the evidence is. Users can discover NASA resources, view a real GISTEMP global-temperature record, import supported CSV or NetCDF data, and explore linked maps and time series. Its Bayesian engine separates seasonal variation from long-term trends, accounts for correlated observations, and reports credible intervals and probabilities of scientifically meaningful change. Regional trends remain visible even when increases and decreases cancel in an overall average. Information-gain estimates identify where an additional observation could most improve understanding. Clearly labeled synthetic Bayesian demonstrations, NASA observational values, reproducible exports, and explicit limitations make the system useful for learning and exploratory research. The project makes environmental change easier to examine without hiding uncertainty behind a single trend line.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Earth System Trend Detective is a local Python application with a browser-based explorer and a command-line interface. It connects a map of observation locations to each location's time series, estimated change, credible interval, and probabilities of increase or decrease beyond a user-selected practical threshold. Users select a quantity, observation period, and geographic region, then switch between effect size, uncertainty, coverage, and provisional evidence map layers. NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) searches help users discover Earth science collections and variable metadata. Supported CSV and rectilinear NetCDF files supply observations or model output. A separately labeled NASA GISTEMP chart displays downloaded global temperature anomalies without inventing uncertainty or a Bayesian significance result. A public website presents a saved analysis, the six-slide demo, and downloadable full source code.

HOW IT ADDRESSES THE CHALLENGE

The system estimates local trends before combining regional summaries, preserving opposite responses in different places even when an overall average approaches zero. A seasonal linear Bayesian model distinguishes recurring annual variation from the long-term rate. Temporally correlated errors and supplied measurement uncertainties account for repeated observations not providing independent evidence. The engine integrates over an explicit finite grid of noise and autocorrelation settings and partially pools slopes within scientifically justified groups. Joint posterior covariance supports weighted regional uncertainty estimates. Results answer the challenge's central questions: which quantity changes, where, how much, and how strongly the model supports a meaningful directional claim. The practical threshold separates a detectable direction from a scientifically relevant effect. Provisional declarations use a bound on the posterior expected proportion of false claims. These are model-dependent Bayesian results, not classical p-values or causal explanations.

CREATIVITY AND EFFICIENCY

The numerical engine uses Kalman innovations and analytic Gaussian calculations instead of sampling every latent time point (about 6 seconds for a 60-location, 20-year example). Content-derived manifests and execution fingerprints support reproducible caching. Changing the practical threshold reuses the existing posterior without refitting. Background jobs provide progress, cancellation, and explicit incomplete states. An information-theory panel estimates how much a hypothetical next observation could reveal about a trend, connecting analysis to where additional evidence would help most.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

The project helps students, educators, and exploratory researchers reason about environmental change with better access to uncertainty and provenance. Unit correctness, pooling groups, spatial support, and missing-data handling are made inspectable so users can investigate a result before relying on it.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, AND SOFTWARE

Python, NumPy, SciPy, FastAPI, Uvicorn, xarray, cftime, h5netcdf, h5py, SQLite, and a local HTML/CSS/JavaScript/SVG interface with no external map services. Playwright drove desktop/mobile browser verification. The project passed 55 automated tests covering independent dense Gaussian reference calculations, opposing trends, missing observations, calendars, quality handling, units, caching, and API behavior. The regional temperature, moisture, and vegetation examples are explicitly synthetic; NASA GISTEMP values remain separately identified as actual observational analysis. Exports record model settings and provenance for reproducibility.
